title: value-mapping-and-pilot-pricing-playbook-2026
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook equips field teams and solution engineers with a repeatable, scalable approach to: (1) map Redwood Inference value to buyer metrics, (2) structure pilot engagements, (3) present competitive tradeoffs, and (4) answer common security and deployment questions during procurement. The goal is to accelerate pilots to a measurable business outcome and a clean path to a commercial contract.

Audience
- AE / SE / Solutions Engineers running technical pilots
- GTM leadership designing proof-of-value (PoV) pipelines
- Customer success teams transitioning pilots to paid accounts

Quick summary (elevator)
- Elevator pitch: Redwood Inference delivers predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes — helping engineering teams reduce per-request cost, stabilize latency, and move from prototype to SLA-backed production quickly.

Use cases & value mapping (how to quantify ROI)
1) Customer Support Automation (SaaS):
   - Prior state: average resolution time 45 minutes; 10% of escalations to human agents; annual NRR impact unknown.
   - Redwood pilot outcome: automate triage and first-response generation, reduce human escalations by 30% and median time-to-first-response to < 2 minutes.
   - Metrics to capture during pilot: automated-resolution-rate, mean time-to-first-response, tokens per session, cost per conversaton.

2) Document Understanding (Enterprise):
   - Prior state: manual extraction pipeline costing $xx per month; ML experiments with inconsistent latency.
   - Redwood pilot outcome: consistent 99th percentile inference latency < 120 ms (for short-doc workflows) and 40% reduction in tooling cost via batching and cache reuse.
   - Metrics: 99p latency, cost per 1k documents, extraction accuracy (precision/recall), throughput (req/s).

3) Personalization & Recommendations (Marketplace):
   - Pilot outcomes: lower latency for real-time reranking, 10% uplift in CTR and measurable revenue impact; adopt dedicated pools for peak windows.
   - Metrics: inference cost per recommendation, latency percentiles, business KPI delta.

Pilot structure (recommended 6-week cadence)
1) Week 0: Alignment & success criteria
   - Deliverables: success metrics (3–5), data access checklist, risk/fallback plan, NDA/POC MOU.
2) Week 1: Lightweight integration
   - Deliverables: API key, sample dataset ingestion, test harness, baseline run (existing model or local baseline).
3) Week 2–3: Optimization & performance tuning
   - Activities: batching and cache rules, model variant selection, quantization recommendations, autoscaling smoke tests.
   - Deliverables: perf dashboard link, SLO targets documented.
4) Week 4: Business validation
   - Activities: A/B tests vs baseline, quality checks, cost-per-unit analysis.
5) Week 5: Security & compliance review
   - Deliverables: deployment mode decision (hosted/dedicated/private), KMS integration plan, SOC2 evidence summary.
6) Week 6: Wrap & commercial proposal
   - Deliverables: pilot report (metrics), recommended committed capacity or hosted tier, SLA/contract template.

Pilot pricing templates (field-useable)
- Small PoV (Developer/Team): 4-week, free compute credit up to $2,500 + technical onboarding (2 SE days) — intent: quick proof-of-value for integration and product-market fit.
- Outcome PoV (Business metric-driven): 6-week engagement with shared success milestones. Pricing: $12k fixed fee + compute burn (billed) with a 50% credit if contract signed w/in 60 days. Includes 5 SE days, priority onboarding, and a cost/performance report.
- Dedicated Pilot (Enterprise & Regulated): 8-week reserved pool with 99.9% uptime target. Pricing: $25k onboarding + minimum monthly commit estimate for reserved GPUs (example: 2x A10G equiv). Migration assistance and optional on-prem packaging at additional cost.

Negotiation levers for AE/SE
- Trade compliance resources for longer-term commitments (e.g., extend onboarding days in exchange for 12-month commit).
- Offer graduated discounts on committed tiers (3–6–12 month).
- Apply one-time migration credit when customers move from hosted to private/dedicated.

Competitive brief (high level)
- Table: competitor | typical customer | differentiation | common pushback
  - Large cloud AI endpoints (C1): Enterprises exploring managed endpoints for model ownership but limited inference cost controls. Differentiation: Redwood offers cost-aware batching, transparent token economics, and predictable dedicated pools. Pushback: they have deeper cloud integration. Response: emphasize our specialized inference kernel selection and SLO-backed dedicated offering.
  - LLM API pure-play (C2): Simpler API, broad model catalog. Differentiation: Redwood focuses on production SLOs, rollout controls, and private deployment. Pushback: they are cheaper for bursty, experimental workloads. Response: position Redwood for production economics and long-term cost predictability; propose hybrid routing to mix both.
  - On-prem inference stack vendors (C3): Full control & air-gapped options but requires heavy integration. Differentiation: Redwood provides a private deployment option with managed control plane and turnkey packaging. Pushback: customers want total control. Response: offer clear migration path + auditability + HSM/KMS integrations.

Competitive objection handling (scripts)
- "Their price is lower for dev use" -> "We support free developer tiers for experimentation. Our value is in the transition to production where unit economics and operational SLOs matter; we model expected savings from caching/batching during the pilot and show concrete per-100k token numbers."
- "We already run models on our infra" -> "If you own infra, we can provide Redwood Private with optional managed services to run the control plane; our runtime specializes in kernel selection and continuous batching that reduces per-token cost compared to generic deployment stacks."

Pitch deck highlights (slide-by-slide for SEs)
1) Problem: unpredictable cost and latency when moving LLMs to production.
2) Why now: models + hardware options create a need for a consistent runtime.
3) Redwood solution: unified API + serving runtime + ops for hosted/dedicated/private.
4) Key differentiators: SLOs, caching, model and quantization recommendations, rolling deployments.
5) Pilot approach: 6-week plan with measurable metrics.
6) Case study: anonymized win (see below).
7) Pricing and next steps: pilot offer and contract path.

Sales-ready case study (concise)
- Customer: anonymized fintech (mid-market)
- Problem: inconsistent latency spikes causing revenue-impacting timeouts in recommender path.
- Pilot: 6-week dedicated pilot with 3-day integration and model routing to lower-cost quantized variant during off-peak.
- Results: 99th percentile latency dropped from 1.2s to 130ms for core flows; inference cost per 100k tokens decreased by 36%; conversion rate on recommendations improved by 7%.
- Impact: customer signed 12-month reserved capacity commitment within 45 days of pilot close.

Security FAQ for prospects (sales-focused answers)
Q: What deployment options protect my sensitive data?
A: We offer three deployment modes: (1) Redwood Hosted (data-in-transit and at-rest encryption, SOC2 controls), (2) Redwood Dedicated (private tenant GPU pools, network isolation, contractually isolated compute), and (3) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem package with optional air-gapped setup). Recommend dedicated/private for regulated data.

Q: How do you handle key management and encryption?
A: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) in major cloud providers and HSM integrations for Private deployments. Keys never leave customer-managed KMS for private mode; for Hosted, we can offer per-customer encryption contexts and rotate keys on customer cadence.

Q: Can I get audit logging and evidence for compliance?
A: Yes — we provide structured audit logs for API calls, model version rollouts, and administrative actions. For enterprise contracts we deliver SOC2 artifacts and can coordinate a security questionnaire (SIG, CORS) response.

Q: What about data residency?
A: Hosted deployments are region-aware and we have region-specific endpoints. Private & Dedicated allow you to select exact region or on-prem locality to meet residency requirements.

Q: Do you retain data used for model improvement?
A: Default: Hosted inference does not use customer request payloads for model training. Any telemetry used for runtime improvements is aggregated and anonymized. For customers requiring stricter controls, Private deployments include contractual guarantees of no training usage and the option to disable telemetry.

Q: What are typical SLOs we can request during a pilot?
A: Example pilot SLOs: 99% p50 < 50 ms (small request), 99% p95 < 200 ms, 99% availability for the dedicated pool. SLOs are tailored per workload and finalized in Week 0.

Security redlines and negotiation notes (for SEs)
- Standard: provide SOC2 Type II, encryption at rest/in transit, role-based access.
- Redlines requiring legal escalation: indemnity caps, data ownership exceptions, or removal of audit rights. Route to the legal Slack channel and CSM for escalation.

Operational checklist for pilots (runbook style)
- Pre-engagement: NDA, API key + scoped service account, baseline dataset, success metric doc.
- Day 0: Create pilot workspace, ingest sample traffic, link to perf dashboards.
- Monitoring: enable token-level cost reporting, latency histograms, and error budgets.
- Escalation: SE oncall -> Solutions Engineering manager -> security contact.

Appendix: sample pilot success metric template (CSV columns)
- metric_name, description, baseline_value, target_value, measurement_method, owner
- Example row: automated_resolution_rate, "% of tickets closed without human intervention", 12%, 30%, webhook + support logs, SE

Appendix: quick rebuttal snippets (copy-paste)
- Customer: "We need the cheapest option."
  SE: "If the immediate priority is lowest upfront cost for experimentation, we support free dev tiers. From a production perspective, we model total cost including stalls, manual ops, and failed rollouts; in many cases Redwood reduces long-term unit costs through caching and better kernel selection."

- Customer: "We have an in-house MLOps platform."
  SE: "Great — Redwood Private can integrate with your infra and provide the runtime advantages (continuous batching, KV cache) while leaving control of the underlying hardware to you. We can scope a hybrid pilot to prove the delta in per-token cost."
